method.method_draft: Use a synthetic right-triangle approach. From the image, note that OC is drawn through D to the lower point C of the circle, and AB is the horizontal chord intersected by OC at D. From the text, C is the midpoint of arc AB, so OC is the perpendicular bisector of chord AB. Therefore AD=DB=4 because AB=8, and CD=2 lies on the same radius line as OC. Let the radius be r, so OC=r and OD=r-2. Connect OA; triangle AOD is right with hypotenuse OA=r and legs AD=4, OD=r-2. Apply Pythagoras: r^2=4^2+(r-2)^2, giving r=5.
